title: King Street East tower and Mill Street referral
subtitle: Also: affordable housing appeal, traffic concerns, and city-wide active transportation route signage and branding.
overview: The Planning and Strategic Initiatives Committee dealt with two development applications and a cycling and trails wayfinding plan. Its decisions are recommendations that Council must still adopt or change.

For 328-330 Mill Street, staff recommended refusing a zoning change for a 20-storey building with reduced bicycle parking and setbacks. The applicant asked for more time to respond to staff comments. The committee recommended referring the matter to the September 30 Council meeting so the applicant can talk further with staff {{vote:m1}}.

For 2980 King Street East, the committee recommended adopting an Official Plan amendment and approving a zoning change for a mixed-use development of 436 homes and 692 square metres of commercial space, up to 27 storeys {{vote:m2}}. The Official Plan amendment would go to the Region of Waterloo for approval. Councillors raised traffic and affordable housing questions.
The committee also directed staff to proceed with a wayfinding strategy and branding for eight city-wide active transportation routes, after more community engagement {{vote:m3}}.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended referring the staff refusal recommendation to the September 30, 2024 Council meeting so the applicant can talk further with staff about the planning comments {{vote:m1}}.

The committee recommended adopting the Official Plan amendment, to be forwarded to the Region of Waterloo for approval, and approving the zoning by-law amendment for a mixed-use development with 436 residential units {{vote:m2}}.
The committee directed staff to proceed with the proposed wayfinding strategy for city-wide active transportation routes following further community engagement {{vote:m3}}.

debate: Mill Street: a nearby resident supported staff's refusal, stressing that one indoor bicycle space per unit matters for car-free living and e-bikes. The resident also urged lower-carbon design, such as no natural gas, on-site energy generation and stormwater retention.

Mill Street: the applicant's planning consultant said the applicant had not had time to address staff comments before the report was finalized, and asked for a deferral. One councillor, a general supporter of housing, warned the proposal was very far from established parameters.

King Street East: one councillor doubted the traffic study, citing other planned developments nearby. Staff said the site sits on two major regional roads with high existing volumes, the Region plans to extend River Road, and parking is reduced with extra bicycle parking.

King Street East: a councillor asked whether affordable housing had been discussed. Staff said it was not requested and that a different builder will likely carry out the project. The councillor appealed to the applicant to consider affordable units, noting no mechanism requires it.

Wayfinding: councillors backed the design but asked staff to consider QR codes, GPS and app integration, naming trails, accessibility beyond colour, lighting on commuter routes, and links to other municipalities. Some felt the 16-year build-out was too long.
